# dte-sdk

> TypeScript SDK for Chilean electronic tax documents (DTE): build, stamp (TED), sign (XMLDSig) and envelope documents for the SII and talk to the SII web services (upload, status, acceptance/claims), with an English domain model, bilingual EN/ES JSDoc and RUT handling delegated to rut.ts.

The package has four entries, ES modules only, on Node ≥ 22.12 (`require()` loads them too): `dte-sdk` (documents, stamps, signatures, envelopes, books, the SII web services client over `fetch` and the public registry of authorized issuers; also runs on Bun and Deno and bundles for the browser), `dte-sdk/node` (`createNodeHttpsTransport`, `createDirectoryCapture`, `createDirectoryUploadArchive`, `createDirectoryTokenCache`, `createDirectoryFolioRegistry`, and the CAF file search `findCafFiles`, `findLatestCafFile`, `resolveCafFile`, `cafFileScope`), `dte-sdk/portal` (the SII portal, folios, the register, the MIPYME backup, the activity verification, the certification sets and the certification runner) and `dte-sdk/pdf` (printed samples and the SII office of each commune, `SII_OFFICES` and `siiOfficeForCommune`; needs the optional peers `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js`). `DteError` and `isDteError` come from `dte-sdk` and recognize what every entry throws.

dte-sdk covers document types 33, 34, 39, 41, 43, 46, 52, 56 and 61. `createDocument` validates and normalizes input (RUTs via rut.ts, text sanitized, schema lengths enforced, totals computed with per-line rounding, VAT-included prices via `MntBruto`, withholding for purchase invoices, receipt defaults). `transport` carries the transport of goods of a dispatch guide or an invoice that moves them, with the fields of Res. Ex. 144/2026 (`trailerLicensePlate`, `departureDate`, `departureTime`, `arrivalDate`), every one optional as `DTE_v10.xsd` declares it and checked before stamping; `options.transferType` takes 1 to 9, the values the schema admits. `commissions` holds the commission and other charge lines of a settlement invoice (43), or of a purchase invoice and the notes that correct one: a line needs `netValue` or `exemptValue` (the one it lacks is written as zero, since the schema requires both), its `vatValue` defaults to its net value by the VAT rate, rounded, and the totals carry in `commissions` (`Totales/Comisiones`) the lines' net and exempt values added up and their VAT, which is the VAT rate by the total net value rounded once (the SII's validation 38 for settlement invoices) or the sum of the lines' VAT when a line states its own, and take them off `totalAmount` (Formato DTE 2.5, field 124), which on a 43 may be zero or negative, as may its net, exempt amount and VAT; explicit `totals` are written as given. A 43 is held to what its root `Liquidacion` declares: `createDocument` refuses `transport`, `globalAdjustments`, line discounts and surcharges, a reference's `otherRut`, `totals.nonBillableAmount` and the options `noDebitReduction`, `dispatchType`, `transferType`, `printFormat`, `exportPaymentTerms` and `netAmountsIndicator` (`INVALID_OPTION`), requires the receiver's `businessActivity` (`MISSING_FIELD`) and admits 60 lines and 20 commissions; `settledDocumentType` (`TpoDocLiq`) is required on its lines and refused on any other type. A receipt (39, 41) is held to its own schema, `EnvioBOLETA_v11.xsd`, much shorter than the invoice's: `createDocument` refuses `transport`, `commissions`, `withholdVat: true`, every `options` field but `serviceIndicator`, `netAmountsIndicator` (only 2), `billingPeriod`, `dueDate` and `paymentMedium`, the totals `vatRate`, `ownVatAmount`, `thirdPartyVatAmount`, `withholdings` and `commissions`, and on a line `referenceQuantity`, `referenceUnit`, `referencePrice`, `additionalTaxCodes` and an `exemptIndicator` other than 1, 2 or 6 (`INVALID_OPTION` with the field in `details.field`); it keeps `globalAdjustments`, `subtotals` and `receiptReferences`; the issuer's `branch`, `phone`, `email`, `activityCode` and `salespersonCode` and the receiver's `businessActivity`, which a receipt has no element for, are left out, not refused, so one issuer serves invoices and receipts, and so are the receiver's `email` and postal address, which its schema declares and dte-sdk does not write yet; `totals.periodAmount` is written as the receipt's `TotalPeriodo` (`MontoPeriodo` on other types); `softwareProviderRut` (`RUTProvSW`, the RUT of the provider of the issuing software, the issuer's own for in-house software) is optional, written only when given, and with `options.netAmountsIndicator` (`IndMntNeto`) is refused on every type that is not a receipt. On a receipt `paymentMedium` must be a number from 1 to 5 as text; that is not checked yet. `toSiiDocument`/`fromSiiDocument` map the English model (`totalAmount`, `issuer.businessName`) to the official SII tags (`MntTotal`, `RznSoc`) in schema order. `stampDocument` builds the exact `<DD>` string and signs it with the CAF private key (SHA1withRSA over ISO-8859-1 bytes). `signDocument` applies the enveloped XMLDSig signature (C14N 1.0, RSA-SHA1) the SII validates. `createEnvelope`/`signEnvelope` produce `EnvioDTE`/`EnvioBOLETA`. Certificates load from PKCS#12 or PEM; CAF files are parsed and checked for range and the 6-month expiry of invoice/note CAFs. `verifyReceivedDocuments(xml, { environment?, siiKeys? })` checks a `DTE`, `EnvioDTE` or `EnvioBOLETA` as received, each document read from its element: the envelope's own signature and, per document, its XMLDSig signature, its TED (`FRMT` with the key of the CAF the TED carries, `DD` against the header), that CAF against the document (issuer, type, folio inside the range) and the SII's `FRMA` over the CAF with the key of its `IDK` (`SII_CAF_KEYS`: 100 certification, 300 production; only the key of `environment`, production by default, is accepted, and a CAF of the other environment is invalid; `verifyCafSignature` checks one CAF, an empty `FRMA` is `invalid`, and `cafEnvironment` reads the environment of an `IDK`); each check is data with a `status` of `valid`, `invalid` or `unchecked` (no key for that `IDK`), and malformed input throws. Status codes from the SII web services are classified (`accepted`, `pending`, `rejected`, `queryError`). Errors are `DteError` with stable codes and no personal data in messages. All clock-dependent functions accept `{ now }`.

The SII web services client is `createSiiClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions: `uploadEnvelope`/`uploadBook`/`uploadFolioConsumption` (DTEUpload multipart in ISO-8859-1, or the receipts REST API in production; the XML must open with a declaration naming ISO-8859-1; duplicates return the original TrackID), `queryUploadStatus`/`waitForUploadStatus`/`queryDocumentStatus`/`folioReceived`, the acceptance/claim registry `registerClaim`/`listClaimEvents`/`queryTransferable`/`queryReceptionDate`/`receiverStatus` (for types `CLAIM_DOCUMENT_TYPES`, 33, 34 and 43, with the guard `isClaimDocumentType`), the pure `receiverAnswer` (the whole `listClaimEvents` result plus reception date plus today: annulled, claimed, accepted, `paidInCash` when the SII marked it paid in cash (`PAG`; the registry refuses events on it with code 27 and there is no deadline), tacitly accepted after 8 calendar days, goods received, pending, or `unknown` when the query failed with no events, and the claim deadline), and `queryAuthorizedIssuer`, the public registry of authorized issuers (resolution number and date of the environment, document types; no certificate or session needed). Tokens are obtained and renewed automatically per environment, channel and certificate. Transport is injectable (`fetch` by default, `createNodeHttpsTransport` from `dte-sdk/node` with TLS verification on; `tls.ca` adds to Node's bundled roots), retries use exponential backoff and never re-send an upload or a claim after an SII answer (not even a partial one), and `capture`/`archive` ports record redacted HTTP exchanges and the bytes of every upload.

The SII books are `createPurchaseSalesBook` (IECV, `LibroCompraVenta`), `createGuideBook` (`LibroGuia`) and `createFolioConsumption` (RCOF, `ConsumoFolios`), each with `build*Xml`, `sign*`, `verify*Signature` and `toSii*`. All submission kinds of the schemas are covered, and the SDK computes the summaries from the lines; `summaryOnlyTotals` and `previousTotals` carry what cannot be derived. An explicit line total that differs from the SII formula is kept and reported in `totalMismatches`, and `strictTotals: true` throws `BOOK_TOTAL_MISMATCH` instead. `bookEntryFromDocument`, `guideEntryFromDocument` and `folioConsumptionEntryFromDocument` derive the lines from issued documents. The signed XML goes to `uploadBook` or `uploadFolioConsumption`. The RCV replaced the IECV in production from period 2017-08, the guide book is sent only on SII request, and the report is used in the receipts certification; the SII probably no longer requires it in production.

Certification (deterministic half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `parseTestSetText` parses the SII test-set text into sets and cases; `planCertificationSets` gives what each set issues and the folios per type; `createFolioAllocator` hands out folios with the CAF that stamps them; `issueTestSet` issues the basic, exempt, guide and purchase sets through phase 1 with the `SET` reference (`CASO <id>`) and the field rules, written in a fixed form (UTC issue day and UTC stamps with milliseconds, unit prices with six decimals, zero totals on the notes that correct a text); `issueSimulation` re-issues every case in one envelope; `createCertificationSalesBook`, `createCertificationPurchaseBook` and `createCertificationGuideBook` build and sign the books through phase 3, as total submissions or adjustments, with fixed lines and summaries (the withheld VAT rate as 0.19, the common-use credit rounded per document). Nothing sends: the runner does.

Certification (portal half, from `dte-sdk/portal`): `runCertification` runs the HTML side in the field's order from a `CertificationStore` (`createMemoryCertificationStore`, `createDirectoryCertificationStore`; the state holds CAF private keys): the test sets, the books, the simulation, the exchange set answered on the exchange portal (`downloadExchangeSet`, `validateExchangeUser`, `uploadExchangeAnswers`, `confirmExchange`; the answers from `createExchangeAnswers`, signed and schema-valid), the printed samples uploaded to the samples portal when the `samples` option gives them (`readPrintedSamples` from `dte-sdk/pdf`; `readSamplesReview`, `createSamplesReview`, `uploadSample`, `submitSamplesReview`, `readSamplesDetail`), and the declaration of compliance, irreversible, only with `declareCompliance: true`; it stops with `exchange` (the set unavailable or the company not in the exchange), `printedSamples` (no samples given), `rejected` (the SII's reasons in the detail) or `compliance`. Each phase is a step over the dependencies and the state (`obtainTestSet`, `prepareFolios`, `sendTestSet`, `declareTestSets`, `waitForTestSetsApproval`, `runBooks`, `advanceToNextStage`, `sendSimulation`, `declareSimulation`, `waitForSimulationApproval`, `runExchange`, `uploadPrintedSamples`, `declareComplianceFinal`), with typed progress events through `onProgress`; beneath them the portal operations `downloadTestSet` (generates the set anew at the SII), `declareProgress` (every field in form order, the page read again to verify), `readProgress`, `advanceStage`, `listBookHistory` and `declareCompliance`. The two GWT portals speak GWT-RPC (`gwtBody`, `gwtAnswer`); the exchange uses the pair of hashes known to work and the samples portal's are discovered once with that pair as the fallback. Each portal is entered once per stage of work (`withExchangeStage`, `withSamplesStage`; the operations take `stage`), its calls are sent once with no time-out of their own and a fixed set of headers, their answers read as UTF-8; any failure of the set download asks for the set by hand, and the set is read loosely. The run keeps to field behaviour in what the SII receives and in how it flows: the declaration carries today's Chile date, the uploads of the run retry only network failures (eight attempts) and take `STATUS` 99 as a failed send, a portal request waits 20 s, and `receiver`, `resolution` and the issuer's activity, commune and city have defaults (`DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_RECEIVER`, `DEFAULT_CERTIFICATION_ISSUER`). The books phase starts over on every run (the period from the UTC month the set was read in, the approved books from the portal), resends as adjustments or in the next free period, and never stops on a portal read; with the three mandatory books sent the runner asks for the next stage and stops with the portal's sentence when it does not move (`runBooks` is `incomplete` only when a mandatory book could not be sent; `advanceToNextStage` returns `advanced`, `unchanged`, `failed` or `timedOut` and never throws for a portal answer). The simulation carries the local date of the process and UTC stamps to the second; the declaration of compliance counts as made when the last page no longer shows its form. Before issuing, the run asks the SII (as the company) whether it already holds the folios it is about to use, uses a range obtained again only through the folios the SII showed free, reads a maximum it cannot read as no cap, never asks for a blocked type and keeps the annulled ranges in the state. The waits are the field's and `sleep` and `now` are injectable. None of it has been run against the portal yet.

Certification of receipts (from `dte-sdk/portal`), an application of its own with no runner, as pieces to chain, kept to field behaviour like the document runner (the set read by position, the UTC day and UTC stamps to the second on the receipts, uploads read and retried as the run's, the portal called with a fixed set of headers, once, 30 s, UTF-8, its states searched in the raw answer; `sendReceiptsSet().envelopeTrackId` is null for a duplicate without a track id): `downloadReceiptsTestSet` (the plain-text set), `parseReceiptsTestSet`, `issueReceiptsSet` (one receipt of type 39 per case to the final consumer, prices with VAT, the reference `SET` / `CASO-<n>`, the signed `EnvioBOLETA`), `sendReceiptsSet` (uploads the envelope, waits 20 s, reads its status, then sends the folio consumption report with the sequence number 100 plus the attempt, up to ten attempts; `sent` unless the envelope is rejected, `envelopeRejected`, or the report cannot be uploaded or is refused for lack of authorisation, `consumptionFailed`), `declareReceiptsTrackId`, then later `readReceiptsStatus` (`readyToDeclare` at `P90`, `declared` at `P91`) and `declareReceiptsCompliance` (irreversible; `provider` is mandatory; the representative is the owner of the session; `alreadyDeclared` and `notReady` are outcomes), and `verifyReceiptsAuthorization` (type 39 among the stamping types of a production client, and the receipts row of the certification progress page; never throws, a form not served is `queryFailed`). A receipt (39, 41) takes `receiptReferences` (`code`, `reason`, optional `documentType` and `folio`), never `references`: the receipts schema has its own `Referencia`, without a date. None of it has been run against the receipts portal yet.

Printed samples (Node only, from `dte-sdk/pdf`): `parsePrintableDocuments` turns any `EnvioDTE`, `EnvioBOLETA`, bare `SetDTE` or bare `DTE` XML into printable documents with each `TED` copied verbatim; `renderPrintedSample` draws one single-page PDF per the SII printed-samples manual (21.5 cm wide, 11 to 33 cm tall, red type box, acknowledgement box and `CEDIBLE` mark on the transferable copy of 33, 34, 43, 46 and sale guides, PDF417 stamp with the signed bytes and its legends); `renderTedBarcode` gives the stamp PNG alone; `renderPrintedSamples` batches envelopes in memory into the test and simulation sets with failures as data; `writePrintedSamples` and `findEnvelopeFiles` do the same over files (`SET-PRUEBAS`, `SET-SIMULACION`). `pdf-lib` and `bwip-js` load on first use.

The SII portal, from `dte-sdk/portal`, is `createPortalClient({ environment, certificate, companyRut })` plus free functions, on Node (client certificate over `https`; TLS 1.2, server verified). The certificate must be enabled as a login method at sii.cl, or the login throws `SII_PORTAL_CERT_NOT_ENABLED`. Session: `openPortalSession`, `closePortalSession`, or on demand; `sessionCache` and `lock` are ports for several replicas. Company data: `fetchCompanyResolution` (per environment), `fetchTaxpayerData`, `fetchIssuerProfile`, `queryCertificationSets`. Folios: `listStampableTypes`, `queryFolioQuota` (`MAX_AUTOR`, `FOLIOS_DISP`; stamps nothing), `requestCaf` (may grant less than asked; read `granted`), `listFolioRanges`, `annulFolios` (explicit scope required; `maxRanges` limits one call; irreversible; counts against the quota for six months), `listReobtainableRanges`, `reobtainCaf` (signs in on demand; a login page in answer is `SII_PORTAL_SESSION_EXPIRED`). Composite flows return refusals as data: `requestCafExact`, `requestCafInBatches`, `reobtainFolios`. Once a folio flow holds something (CAFs, or folios the SII annulled), any other `DteError` of a later step comes back as data too, in `failure: { code, operation, rejection? }`, and is logged redacted: `requestCafInBatches` and `reobtainFolios` return their CAFs, `annulFolios` and `requestCafExact` their `knownAnnulled`; persist `knownAnnulled` either way; a range its keys cover, in one key or several, is not posted again. A refusal after a grant keeps its kind; only `quotaExceeded` reads as `quotaCapReached`. `portalMessage` is redacted. Refusals are `SII_PORTAL_REJECTED` with `details.rejection` and `portalRejectionMessage`. `createFolioRegistry`, `createMemoryFolioRegistry` and `createDirectoryFolioRegistry` (owner-only `folios.json`) track folios locally. The CAF XML holds a private key: treat it as a secret. `unstable_replenishFolios` (unstable: its shape may change in any release; not run against the SII yet, in either environment) keeps a type stocked in one call: below `minimum` usable folios it downloads again the authorized ranges nobody holds, requests what is missing in batches and annuls as a last resort (certification only unless `allowAnnul`; never a CAF held or a range the run downloaded; only when `FOLIOS_DISP` is over the folios in hand; ranges of the last 180 days). It needs `cafs` (every CAF held, with its unused folios) and `lastIssuedFolio`, stores nothing, returns `status` (`none`, `coolDown`, `replenished`, `partial`, `blocked`, `failed`) with `cafs`, and `coolUntil` and `knownAnnulled` to pass back, and hands what it obtains to `onObtained` with the portal lock held. `planFolioReplenishment` is its decision with no I/O; `reason` is the cause (`low`, `exhausted`, `expired`).

The purchase and sales register runs on the portal session: `listPeriodDocuments`, `fetchRegisterSummary`, `listPurchaseTypes`, `fetchPurchaseDocument`. `REGISTER_DOCUMENT_CODES` and `registerDocumentCode(code)` describe the 49 document codes of the register (sides, DTE, sign, per-document, buyer withholds VAT) and `REGISTER_ACCOUNTING_STATUSES` the statuses of each side. Response codes are not looked at, so a refused month reads as empty; rows have typed fields, `null` when absent, and `raw`. Writes on a production client change the real register: `changePurchaseType`, `moveVatToCommonUse`, `moveVatToRecoverable` are one attempt each, confirmed only by the SII's `OK`; on `purchaseChangeNotConfirmed` the change may have applied, so read the document again before retrying, and VAT amounts are final amounts, not a delta. `downloadMipymeBackup` reads the XML from production whatever the client's environment, in pieces of at most 20 documents, newest first, in the result or through `onChunk`. A day that cannot be downloaded throws before any download. Known defect: a two-day range over 20 documents downloads only its first day, while `total` counts both.

The activity verification runs on the portal session too, and reads production whatever the client's environment: `unstable_fetchActivityVerification` (unstable: its shape may change in any release; read once against the real SII, for a pending verification) gives the company's `requests` (number, kind, reason, `preliminaryResult`, `finalResult`, `status`, `statusDescription`, `requestedOn`, `accreditationDeadline`, `procedureStatus`, `hasCertificate`) and the SII's `messages` (`text`, `blocking`), never officials, comments or the address; it sends the company's RUT, and a request of another RUT throws `SII_PORTAL_UNEXPECTED_PAGE` with `step: 'otherTaxpayer'`; an SII error code throws `activityVerificationRefused`. `listAccreditationDocuments` gives the documents the SII takes to accredit an activity (`category` `general` or `specific`, `code`, `description`; codes repeat across categories).
